exact_items: review record likely needs: review_id, review kind (package review, seam review, verifier/reviewer review), target scope refs, requested/effective reviewer identity, review criteria/profile, findings summary, finding refs / concern refs, verdict / decision, linked artifacts/evidence, timestamps
review findings may nominate or update concerns, but the review record itself should remain distinct from concern records
Corroboration likely wants at least two layers: corroboration_request / packet, corroboration_result
Packet should carry: claim/issue under test, target scope, why corroboration was triggered, evidence set / source refs, required quorum model, participating actor refs
Result should carry: participant outputs, quorum result, accepted / not accepted / advisory-only result, resulting concern/promotion/patch implications
Graph patch likely needs: graph_patch_request, graph_patch_result
Request should carry: patch point, triggering issue/concern refs, requested structural change summary, affected generation, requester identity
Result should carry: old generation, new generation, invalidated path refs, new path refs, surviving/rejoined path refs, resulting concern/promotion/recovery implications

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Promotion record structure including revocation lineage
exact_items: Promotion record should include: promotion class (lane_to_package, package_to_seam, seam_completion), source scope and target scope refs, eligibility state at decision time, blocking refs / concern refs, review/corroboration refs, decision outcome, revocation/reopen lineage if it later changes

Recovery record likely needs: recovery kind (safe-point restore, restart reconciliation, blocked prerequisite resolution, lane/worktree restore), target scope refs, trigger reason, preconditions, result, resulting attempt/run linkage, affected concern refs

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Shared record-envelope pattern across governance/runtime records
exact_items: Candidate shared envelope fields: record_id, record_kind, project_id, run_id?, scope refs (seam_id?, package_id?, node_id?, attempt_id?, promotion_id?, concern_id?, lane_id?, worktree_id?), status, created_at_utc, created_by_kind, created_by_ref?, superseded_by_record_id?, source_refs[], artifact_refs[], evidence_refs[], summary, detail_ref?

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Artifact vs record distinction in export
exact_items: record = canonical structured object in Ledger/export/search/routing
artifact = file/blob/renderable output linked from the record
review markdown summary = artifact, review record = structured ledger object
corroboration packet JSON/markdown = artifact, corroboration result record = structured object

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Exact minimum shapes for all major record families
exact_items: Define exact minimum shapes for: review, corroboration request/result, graph patch request/result, promotion, recovery, state transition report
Keep file/blob artifacts linked to records, not substituted for records

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Export contract split into record/bundle/view categories
exact_items: record export = exact structured object(s), canonical ids, references, metadata
bundle export = manifest + records + attached artifacts/blobs/files
view export = user-facing convenience representation of the current filtered table/list/chart

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Orchestrator export families and manifest requirements
exact_items: Likely export families needed: Evidence export, Artifact export, Ledger export, Run export, Record export for single exact records
Ledger export should be record-shaped first, CSV/JSON second
Run export should include a manifest that ties together: run metadata, exact records, linked artifacts/evidence, historical/superseded status flags

Escalation levels: info, warning, attention_required, blocked, system_notification
History receives everything chronologically
Progress / Dashboard show active warnings / attention / blocked states
badges show compressed counts/severity markers
chat/thread surfaces only for things that genuinely need user decision/input
system notifications reserved for high-value, sparse events
There is no one explicit cross-surface escalation contract yet
Existing banners/cards/toasts/badges are good pieces but not yet tied to a shared cadence model
Rate-limit warning suppression exists conceptually, but comparable suppression/resurfacing rules are less clear for other condition classes

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Blocker demotion rule: attention_required vs blocked must stay distinct
exact_items: attention_required and blocked must remain distinct everywhere
resurfacing should respond to meaningful change, not spam the user on every scheduler tick
the system should not silently demote a persistent blocker into history just because time passed

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Orchestrator-wide scale contract gap for all dense tabs
exact_items: no explicit Orchestrator-wide rule yet for: initial slice size, paging/search interplay, lazy expansion behavior, cross-tab inspector loading strategy, projection fallback behavior under large degraded datasets
scale contract for Seams, Evidence, History, and Ledger much weaker than graph-scale guidance

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Scale exactness vs materialization: paging compatible with exactness
exact_items: exact record inspection in Ledger still needs paging; exactness does not require eager full materialization
historical graph generations must stay accessible without becoming the default visual density
non-graph tabs may become the actual scaling bottleneck sooner than the graph canvas

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Command palette safety policy gap for Orchestrator actions
exact_items: Current docs do not yet define which Orchestrator actions are: palette-visible, shortcut-worthy, context-menu only, bulk-safe, bulk-forbidden
Current grouped/bulk navigation wording could be misread as license for broad bulk execution controls

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Palette confirmation strength must not downgrade across surfaces
exact_items: palette visibility must not silently downgrade confirmation strength
bulk actions should be far narrower than bulk navigation
context menus are likely the cleanest home for exact object-valid live actions
There is no shared freshness/trust contract yet for Orchestrator tabs
Some current wording still risks implying that if data is visible, it is safe to act on it, which is not defensible once projections can lag or degrade

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Stale visibility is not action authority
exact_items: stale visibility is not the same as action authority
blocked/recovery controls are especially sensitive because allowed_action_ids[] can go invalid if projection trust drops
Ledger and record inspectors should be the stable fallback when summary surfaces lose trust
